info.title: BRE Control Plane API
info.description:
Authoring, reviewing, approving and deploying credit policy. This is the control plane — it is NOT the Decision API.

**Two things to know before you integrate.**

**1. This is not where decisions are made.** Decisions come from the decision-service (`POST /v1/decisions`), whose contract is published separately as `decision-api.openapi.yaml`. Everything here is about the policy a decision is made *with*. `POST /v1/policies/{code}/versions/{version}/run` looks like a decision endpoint and is not: it evaluates a DRAFT against facts you supply, stores nothing, and its result is not a decision anybody can be held to.

**2. Authentication establishes who; authorisation comes from this installation.** Present either a session token from `POST /v1/auth/login` or your identity provider's JWT. In both cases the tenant and the roles come from this installation's own tables, never from a header or a token claim — so a valid IdP token for a subject nobody here has provisioned is a 401, not a 200 with no permissions. Every endpoint needs a specific capability, and a 403 names the one you are missing and which roles grant it.

**Segregation of duties is enforced, not advisory.** A version's editor cannot review it; a deployment's approver can be neither the author, nor the reviewer, nor the requester. Those are database constraints and triggers, so a client that works around the UI still cannot work around them. Plan your integration test users accordingly — the commonest first failure is one service account trying to do all three.

bearer.description: A session token from POST /v1/auth/login, or your identity provider's access token. Both go in the same header.
